template: distinguish templates with identical contents but different destinations or sources (#2096)

Consul Template should distinguish templates that have the same body but
different sources or destinations. In cases where a slice of templates is
submitted to the runner with same contents and a dependency, templates with the
same contents body will effectively be "merged" into one.

Nomad templates behave in unpredictable ways when parsing variables outside of
with blocks. See hashicorp/nomad#27455 for more context, but the gist of the
issue is that Consul Template returns pointer values when parsing map items,
and it should instead always return map values.

Prevent path redirection in writeToFile via symlinked path components 

* Prevent path redirection in writeToFile via symlinked path components

writeToFile opened the final user-supplied path directly with os.Create/os.OpenFile, following symlinks in both the parent directory and the final filename. This allowed template output to be redirected outside the intended directory or to clobber an existing file. Reject symlinked parent and final path components using os.Lstat before opening, and route all write, chown, and chmod operations through the validated path.

* template: harden writeToFile against symlink TOCTOU on open and metadata

Open the destination with O_NOFOLLOW so the open fails if the final path
component is a symlink, closing the TOCTOU window between the pre-check and
the open. Apply ownership and permissions via the open file descriptor
(f.Chown/f.Chmod) instead of the path so metadata always targets the file we
opened. O_NOFOLLOW is provided per-platform (no-op on Windows).

* template: only create parent dir when it does not exist

Gate MkdirAll on os.IsNotExist so writeToFile only creates the parent
directory when it is genuinely missing, and surfaces other stat errors
(e.g. permission denied) directly instead of masking them with a MkdirAll
failure.

* template: fail closed when the target path cannot be stat'd

Return early if os.Lstat on the destination fails for any reason other than
the file not existing (e.g. permission denied), rather than proceeding to
open. This keeps the final-component check consistent with the parent
directory check above and avoids continuing when we cannot verify the
target is safe.

Introduce a tls.Config field on VaultConfig (#2168)

Introduce a `TLSConfig *tls.Config` field on `VaultConfig` that allows
callers to supply a pre-built TLS configuration instead of using the
file-based SSL config fields. This is intended for programmatic use cases
(e.g. agent-side TPM integration) where TLS material is not available on
disk.
